cold_open.hook: Meta down 9.65%, Microsoft up 15.33%—the AI trade just split the market in half, and one side is getting left at the station.

markets.macro_note: Risk-on day with a sharp AI divergence: mega-cap AI winners running, Meta stumbling on enterprise messaging and regulatory headwinds.

big_story.story_title: Meta tanks 9%, continuing record losing streak, while Microsoft jumps 14% as AI trade splits
big_story.angle: The market is no longer betting on Meta's AI future—it's betting against it. Earnings miss, FTC lawsuit, and Zuckerberg's vague enterprise AI pitch left investors with no reason to stay.

quick_hits.angle: FTC sues Hims & Hers for selling patient medical data to Meta and Snap—the telehealth unicorn learned that 'privacy' and 'ad targeting' are not compatible business models.
Zoox clears final federal hurdle for paid robotaxi service—the Amazon-owned robo-taxi is now legal to operate, but still has to prove it can actually make money without crashing into a fire hydrant.
Ferrari raises 2026 guidance after Q2 beat—luxury goods holding up while tech implodes, because apparently billionaires still want fast cars even when the AI bubble deflates.
Robinhood's crypto trading revenue plunges 38%—retail crypto enthusiasm is cooling faster than Elon's attention span, and the app that gamified stonks is feeling the pain.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Holidaymakers warned about 'explosive diarrhoea' cyclospora parasite—the parasite has better branding than most crypto projects and a more reliable user base.

yesterday_callback.topic: Investors are selling Meta as it heads to its earnings report
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Yesterday we said they'd sell into earnings. Today they sold THROUGH earnings—and kept selling. The stock is now in freefall, not just a pre-earnings hedge.
